# dustinedwards.info

> Dustin Edwards, Professor and Virologist, Department of Biological Sciences, Tarleton State University. Research in retroviruses and bacteriophages; also builds software on Cloudflare.

Every page below has a markdown twin at its path plus .md. The sections after the link lists, under Optional, explain how search, papers, feeds and the twins work.

## Research

- [Research](https://dustinedwards.info/research): the hub: HTLV-1 and avian retroviruses, bacteriophage research in Texas and science education
- [Retrovirus research](https://dustinedwards.info/research/retroviruses): HTLV-1, REV and LPDV
- [Human retrovirus research: HTLV-1](https://dustinedwards.info/research/retroviruses/human): plain-language summaries of the HTLV-1 papers
- [REV and LPDV in wild turkeys in Texas](https://dustinedwards.info/research/retroviruses/avian): a plain-language guide to two bird retroviruses
- [Bacteriophage research](https://dustinedwards.info/research/bacteriophages): discovery of Microbacterium and Mycobacterium phages, phage genomics and structure
- [Science education research](https://dustinedwards.info/research/science-education): course-based undergraduate research experiences and SEA-PHAGES teaching
- [Publications](https://dustinedwards.info/research/publications): peer-reviewed work, filterable and searchable
- [Our phages](https://dustinedwards.info/research/phages): every bacteriophage isolated in the Tarleton SEA-PHAGES lab since 2017

## Protocols

- [Lab protocols](https://dustinedwards.info/research/protocols): the protocol library
- [Phage Isolation and Purification Protocol](https://dustinedwards.info/research/protocols/phage-isolation): direct and enriched isolation, purification, spot titer, webbed plates, high titer lysate
- [Phage DNA Extraction Protocol](https://dustinedwards.info/research/protocols/phage-dna-extraction): zinc chloride precipitation and TES, with no kit or column
- [COI primers: LCO1490 and HCO2198](https://dustinedwards.info/research/protocols/coi-primers): COI barcoding PCR of invertebrate mitochondrial DNA
- [REV and LPDV PCR primers](https://dustinedwards.info/research/protocols/rev-lpdv-primers): sequences, reaction mix, cycling and product sizes
- [Pan-avian GAPDH PCR](https://dustinedwards.info/research/protocols/pan-avian-gapdh): a control that a bird DNA extraction holds amplifiable avian DNA

- [Lab registry](https://dustinedwards.info/research/lab): the lab's reference catalog of primers, with the phages it has isolated; each primer is /research/lab/primers/<id> with its sequence, computed length and melting temperature, and the protocols that use it, each strain is /research/lab/strains/<id>, the reagents are one table at /research/lab/reagents (supplier, catalog number, link and the protocols that use each), and every registry page has a markdown twin at its path plus .md

A protocol is /research/protocols/<slug>, for example /research/protocols/phage-isolation. Its markdown twin is the same path plus .md.

## Lab calculators

Each states its formula and a worked example.

- [Phage Lab Calculators](https://dustinedwards.info/research/tools): the hub
- [Phage Titer Calculator](https://dustinedwards.info/research/tools/titer): titer in pfu/ml from a plaque count, for a full plate or spot titer
- [Serial Dilution Planner](https://dustinedwards.info/research/tools/dilution): plan a serial dilution of a lysate to a target concentration
- [Webbed Plate Calculator](https://dustinedwards.info/research/tools/webbed-plate): which dilution and how much lysate to plate, and what flooding gives back
- [MOI Calculator](https://dustinedwards.info/research/tools/moi): multiplicity of infection
- [Efficiency of Plating Calculator](https://dustinedwards.info/research/tools/eop): EOP on a test host from titers or plaque counts
- [Lysate Volume Planner](https://dustinedwards.info/research/tools/lysate-volume): how much lysate a set of webbed plates needs

## Teaching

- [Teaching](https://dustinedwards.info/teaching): the hub: Tarleton SEA-PHAGES teaching and undergraduate research in biology
- [Phage Discovery Program](https://dustinedwards.info/teaching/phage-discovery): the two-semester HHMI SEA-PHAGES program, the courses and how students join
- [Student roster](https://dustinedwards.info/teaching/phage-discovery#roster): the roster, on the program page (/phage-discovery 301s there)
- [Virus Isolation Course](https://dustinedwards.info/teaching/virus-isolation): students isolate bacteriophages from soil, purify and image them, and extract phage DNA
- [Lab Calculations and Common Questions](https://dustinedwards.info/teaching/virus-isolation/faq): worked phage lab calculations from the virus isolation course
- [Phage Bioinformatics Course](https://dustinedwards.info/teaching/phage-bioinformatics): annotating a phage genome in PHEONA, step by step
- [Central Dogma Tutorials](https://dustinedwards.info/teaching/central-dogma): replication, transcription, translation and the genetic code
- [Study Skills Guide](https://dustinedwards.info/teaching/study-skills): learning styles, the VARK model and what research says

## Software

A page is /software/{name}. /projects 301s to /software.

- [Software](https://dustinedwards.info/software): the hub
- [Foxhound](https://dustinedwards.info/software/foxhound): recovers failed Stripe subscription payments and replaces Recova; live at https://foxhoundapp.com
- [Foxing](https://dustinedwards.info/software/foxing): a reading application for public-domain books; live at https://foxing.app
- [Foxing Edu](https://dustinedwards.info/software/foxing-edu): a separate product built on Foxing and sold to schools; no public address is recorded here
- [Germomics](https://dustinedwards.info/software/germomics): a narrative podcast on microbiology and its history; live at https://germomics.com
- [Capsid](https://dustinedwards.info/software/capsid): infrastructure: versioned markdown in namespaces, with typed edges and search; this site's rulings live in it
- [Enarratio](https://dustinedwards.info/software/enarratio): an open-source chart library in early alpha, at https://github.com/DrDustinEdwards/enarratio with a gallery at https://enarratio.dustinedwards.info
- [Carrel](https://dustinedwards.info/software/carrel): the private writing hub this site's articles are written in; it has a page but no public app address
- [Capsomer](https://dustinedwards.info/software/capsomer): the shared design system of plain-CSS components, color tokens and page patterns these apps are built from; its home is https://capsomer.dustinedwards.info

TXASM (https://txasm.org) is a site of Dustin's and has no page on this site. This site is described at the [colophon](https://dustinedwards.info/colophon). The lab tools are listed above under Lab calculators. Each of the Capsid, Enarratio, Carrel and Capsomer pages opens with a dictionary entry for its name.

## Writing

- [Writing](https://dustinedwards.info/writing): every article, filterable by tag at /writing?tag=<tag>
- [RSS feed](https://dustinedwards.info/writing/rss.xml): the feed at /writing/rss.xml
- [JSON feed](https://dustinedwards.info/writing/feed.json): the feed at /writing/feed.json
- [Full text of every post](https://dustinedwards.info/llms-full.txt): every published post in one file, /llms-full.txt

An article is /writing/<slug>. Its markdown twin is /writing/<slug>.md. Requesting the article URL with Accept: text/markdown returns the same markdown.

## Optional

### Markdown twins

Every research, teaching and software page, each lab calculator and the CV has a markdown twin at its path plus .md, for example /research.md, /research/tools/titer.md, /software/enarratio.md and /cv.md. The HTML head links it with rel="alternate" type="text/markdown". The twin's Link header names the HTML page as canonical. Article URLs also answer Accept: text/markdown. Paper twins and article twins use the patterns above and below. Twins are not in the sitemap.

### About the site

The sections above are the map. The rest of this file is how search, papers and feeds work.

### Colophon

/colophon describes how this site is built: every Cloudflare binding with the
measurement that put it there, the schema migrations, the build gates, the
runtime dependencies, and what was deliberately not adopted and why. The stack
half is generated from the repository's own configuration and reconciled
against it by a build gate rather than maintained by hand.

### How it looks

The look is a fixed direction rather than a theme that drifts per page. It
is Swiss editorial on warm limestone paper: ink text, 1px hairlines as the only
structure, and one accent colour used as ink for links and focus rather than as
a fill. Titles and prose are a serif, and dates, identifiers and counts are a
monospace, so the machine-readable values on a page are the ones set in mono.
The rule is ruled rows rather than cards, no filled public control, no capsule
and no tracked capitals. The post page and the home page are rebuilt under that
rule; the index pages still carry the older vocabulary and are being brought to
it, so a page that contradicts this paragraph is behind, not an exception. The
theme is an attribute and follows prefers-color-scheme when none is set.

The half of that which never degrades is the machine half. Every public page
renders its content, data, citations, dates and structure in server HTML,
complete and correct without script, and keeps its markdown twin, its entry in
this file, its JSON-LD and its microformats. No public route hydrates and no
framework runs on a reading page. The script that does load is hand-written and
adds only what a person would want, such as zooming a figure or filtering
without a reload, and a filter writes the query string, so a URL you are handed
shows you what it showed whoever sent it.

### Writing, in detail

Posts are listed at /writing and can be filtered by tag at /writing?tag=<tag>.
Every post has a plain markdown twin at /writing/<slug>.md, which is the source
the page was rendered from. Requesting /writing/<slug> with an
Accept: text/markdown header returns the same markdown. The feed is at
/writing/rss.xml and /writing/feed.json.

### Publications

Peer-reviewed work is listed at /research/publications, filterable by topic at
/research/publications?topic=<topic> and searchable at /research/publications?q=<query>. Every
filter and every search is an ordinary GET, so each view is a real URL.

Each paper has its own page at /research/publications/<doi-slug>/, where the slug is the
DOI with every run of punctuation folded to a hyphen: 10.1128/mra.00888-24
becomes /research/publications/10-1128-mra-00888-24/. The page carries the title, the
full author list, the abstract in visible text, the venue, the DOI, PMC and
preprint links where they exist, open-access status, and a citation count from
OpenAlex labelled with the date it was read. Where the licence permits and the
file is hosted here, the PDF sits beside the page at
/research/publications/<doi-slug>/<doi-slug>.pdf.

Citations export as files rather than as a copy button:

- [BibTeX, the whole list](https://dustinedwards.info/research/publications.bib): /research/publications.bib
- [RIS, the whole list](https://dustinedwards.info/research/publications.ris): /research/publications.ris
- [CSL JSON, every record](https://dustinedwards.info/research/publications.json): /research/publications.json, including the three conference abstracts the page does not show
- One paper as BibTeX: /research/publications/<slug>.bib
- One paper as RIS: /research/publications/<slug>.ris

The bibliographic data is from Crossref and DataCite, with abstracts backfilled
from Europe PMC where a publisher deposited none. Counts are OpenAlex.

Every paper also has a markdown twin at /research/publications/<doi-slug>.md. It carries the
record as YAML frontmatter, the abstract, and, where the PDF is hosted here,
the machine-extracted text of that PDF. That is the form to read if you are a
program: the page says those things across HTML, meta tags and a JSON-LD block,
and the twin says them once. The twins are kept out of the search index, like
this file, so the paper's own page is the one that gets indexed.

### Research and teaching pages

The research programme, the lab protocols and the courses are ordinary pages,
written in markdown and rendered to HTML when the site is built. Each has a
markdown twin at the same path plus .md, linked from the page head. Every one
of them is listed in the sections above. The other pages are the home page,
about, writing, software, colophon, contact and privacy, and
[/sitemap.xml](https://dustinedwards.info/sitemap.xml) lists every HTML page on the
site and nothing else.

### Search

[/search?q=<query>](https://dustinedwards.info/search) searches the whole site and returns a normal HTML page.

The same URL returns JSON when requested with Accept: application/json. It is
the same query against the same index, not a separate API, and the response
varies on Accept. Parameters: q, type, tag, year, page. Operators inside q:
tag:<tag>, type:<type>, "quoted phrases", and a bare four-digit year, which is
read as a date filter rather than as text.

Results are section-grained: a hit carries the heading it was found under and a
url with that anchor, so a citation can point at the passage rather than the
page. Each result reports what it matched on (title, tag, body, or filter, the
last meaning the query was a bare year or tag with no text to match).

For programmatic use prefer the JSON form. It is keyword search over an FTS5
index: deterministic, the same query returning the same results, with no model
in the path and no per-request cost.

### Search over MCP

The same corpus is exposed as a Model Context Protocol endpoint, so an agent can
search this site as a tool without scraping it:

- [Search MCP endpoint](https://2795d719-a4de-4558-9322-8fced66a48e6.search.ai.cloudflare.com/mcp): no authentication, one tool, "search"

Results carry the same section-grained keys the rest of the site uses:
blog/<slug>.md is a whole post and blog/<slug>__<anchor>.md is one heading
within it, which maps back to /writing/<slug>#<anchor>.

This is semantic retrieval and it is not the same thing as the JSON endpoint
above. It finds passages that answer a question phrased in a sentence, and it
misses short exact tokens that the keyword index finds immediately. Neither
covers the other, so for a known term use the JSON search and for a question use
this.

Three ways in, then: a URL for people, JSON for programs, MCP for agents.

[/llms-full.txt](https://dustinedwards.info/llms-full.txt) carries every published post in markdown in one document.
